narrative.overview:
RetCalc reads like a well-made Apple settings screen with a financial answer at the top: a soft gray page, white rounded cards that float on it without an edge, big figures in the system face, and controls that everyone already knows how to use (pill buttons, iOS segmented switches, round-thumb sliders, grouped lists with the label left and the value right). Nothing is decorative. Glass, meaning frosted translucency, is used only for things that float over the page: the pinned title bar, the phone tab bar, tips and the bar's hover readout.

The system is calm and dense at once. The page answers first in a large figure, then lays the supporting figures side by side on shared rows, so two cards next to each other line up exactly. Explanations are one tap or hover away in ⓘ tips rather than printed under every number. One amber tint marks what is yours and what is selected; every other color means a kind of money, and means the same kind everywhere.

Light mode is a gray ground with white surfaces and soft shadows. Dark mode is true black with flat gray tonal steps and no card shadows. Both are designed, neither is derived by inverting the other.
keyCharacteristics: Gray ground (#f5f5f7 / #000), white borderless cards with a soft shadow in light, flat tonal steps in dark.
SF Pro on Apple devices, Inter elsewhere; tabular figures throughout; large titles and big secondary figures.
iOS controls: pill buttons, segmented switches with a white knob, round-thumb sliders, grouped inset lists.
One amber tint for the key figure, links in running text, selected states and sliders.
One color per kind of money, on every page, from one map.
Explanations in ⓘ tips; hover lights the chart part and its key entry.
Fields that plainly look fillable, in a column that fits the window and scrolls on its own.

rules.name: The One Tint Rule
rules.body: Amber is the one accent: the key figure, links in running text, selected and current states, and slider fills. It is never a heading, a decoration, an icon at rest or a chart category. If something is amber, it is either the answer, yours, chosen, or a link.

rules.name: The One Color per Money Rule
rules.body: Each kind of money has one color, from the `--c-*` map, on every page, chart, bar, key and table group. Never pick a chart color by hand; never reuse a money color for something that isn't that money. Unassigned money is hatched gray, not a hue.

rules.name: The On Page Rule
rules.body: Text set straight on the gray ground uses On Page, darker than the Muted used for captions inside a white card, because the ground is darker than the card.

rules.name: The Off Is Gray, On Is Clear Rule
rules.body: Things that are off may be gray (Muted text, an outlined row). Things that are on must read at full strength: Text color, a white row, the amber ring or wash. Never gray out something that is in effect.

rules.name: The Never Alone Rule
rules.body: Color never carries meaning by itself. A status is an icon (check or alert) with a label beside it; a money color always has a key entry with a name; a loss has its minus sign.

rules.name: The 4.5 Rule
rules.body: Every text/background pair in both themes clears 4.5:1, including tinted badges; marks that carry meaning (field edges, chart parts, the logo) clear 3:1.

rules.name: The Twelve Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing on screen is set under 12px. Sizes below it are raised with `max(12px, …)`, never left as they were.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number is set with tabular figures: figures, tables, inputs, keys, tips. A number that shifts width as it changes is a bug.

rules.name: The Per Year Rule
rules.body: In sentences and labels write "per year" and "per month", never "a year" or "a month". The short "/yr" and "/mo" are allowed only in a tight figure row, and only when the long unit won't fit. A unit never sits alone on a line: the row goes short, and if it still won't fit, every unit in the row moves under its figure together.

rules.name: The One Line Label Rule
rules.body: Every label fits on one line. Use the short name on the page ("FICA", "Savings rate") and spell it out in its tip ("Social Security and Medicare").

rules.name: The Fits the Window Rule
rules.body: The inputs column is sticky beside the results and never taller than the window: its height runs from where it starts on screen to the window's bottom (less the pinned bar), and it scrolls on its own, so the last input is never a trip to the page's end.

rules.name: The Symmetry Rule
rules.body: Things that can line up do. Cards side by side share rows, labels fit one line so figures sit on one shared line, and there is no needless white space: fill a row side by side before stacking.

rules.name: The No Stacked Shadows Rule
rules.body: A card inside a card is flat with a Rule edge, and a tile that holds a whole tool loses its own frame. Shadows never stack.

rules.name: The Frost Floats Rule
rules.body: Frosted glass is for things that float over the page. A card, a group or the page itself is never frosted, and there are no gradient washes or glows behind the page.

rules.name: The Fillable Rule
rules.body: Anything you can type in or choose must look like it: a white field with a visible Rule Strong edge, in a white group on the gray page; choices show in the tint with a chevron. A gray group or an edgeless field reads as switched off.

rules.name: The Tip, Not Paragraph Rule
rules.body: Explanations live in ⓘ tips. Nothing that has an ⓘ also gets a paragraph under it; cut the on-page copy and let the tip carry it.

rules.name: The Hover Answers Rule
rules.body: Hover always does something useful: an ⓘ opens its tip (focus does the same, a click pins it for touch), and a chart part or its key entry lights both and shows its figures while the rest dims.

dos: Do make every input look fillable: a white field with a visible Rule Strong edge in a white group on the gray page, choices shown in the tint.
Do keep the inputs column sticky, no taller than the window, scrolling on its own.
Do open tips on hover and focus (click to pin), and light a chart part and its key entry together on hover.
Do put side-by-side cards on shared rows so their figures and bars sit level, and fill a row side by side before stacking.
Do use short one-line labels ("FICA") with the full name in the ⓘ tip.
Do show a status as a check or alert icon beside its label, with its sentence on hover.
Do take every money color from the `--c-*` map, and hatch unassigned money gray.
Do set text on the page ground in On Page and captions in a card in Muted.
Do write "per year" and "per month" in sentences; use "/yr" and "/mo" only in a tight figure row.
Do set every number with tabular figures in SF Pro or Inter, and nothing under 12px.
Do keep the Guide report, print summary and share card on their own fixed palettes.
donts: Don't put an explanatory paragraph under anything that has an ⓘ.
Don't give a unit a line of its own: shorten the row's units, then stack them all.
Don't gray out something that is on; only off things may be gray.
Don't use amber for headings, decoration, icons at rest or chart categories.
Don't reuse a money color for something that isn't that money, or pick chart colors by hand.
Don't outline cards, nest a card with a shadow inside another, or stack shadows.
Don't frost anything that doesn't float, or put gradient washes or glows behind the page.
Don't show money taken out in red; use its minus sign. Red is for short and over the limit.
Don't use a gray input group or a borderless field for something you can type in; it reads as switched off.
Don't redraw, recolor or restyle the brand mark.
Don't let a theme change leak into the print summary, the share card or the Guide report.
Don't use hype, gamification (points, badges, streaks, confetti), money emoji, or stock photos of retirees.
